open_points.subject: build_budget_view
open_points.text: - build_budget_view: [PROVENANCE] MUST derive all section and total fields at read time from the selected or active BudgetVersion with its plans, the included expenses and the progress records, taking the section rows from _project_budget_sections; it MUST NOT persist totals.
open_points.other_text: - BudgetVersion fields (exact, no others exist): activated_at: datetime | None, activated_by: UUID | None, created_at: datetime, created_by_id: UUID, created_by_kind: ActorKind, deactivated_at: datetime | None, project_id: UUID, snapshot_id: UUID | None, source: BudgetSource, status: BudgetVersionStatus, version_id: UUID
open_points.question: Must the requirement refer to the plans of a BudgetVersionDetail, or state that the plans are read separately, since BudgetVersion has no plans field?

open_points.subject: build_project_overview
open_points.text: - build_project_overview: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] MUST map each pair from what its builder or reader did: a ScopedNotFoundError means that part is not configured, so the availability is the not_configured member of = models.ViewAvailability and the value is None; a persistence or registry failure means its temporarily_unavailable member and the value None; only a returned projection is its available member. This mapping governs the project pair exactly as it governs the other five: a get_project_context that fails assigns the temporarily_unavailable member to project_availability and None to project, and MUST NOT stop the five component pairs from reporting what their own builders returned, because a registry outage leaves the budget, expenses, progress, payments and photos readable and the client is entitled to them. It MUST NOT let either failure escape to the caller and MUST NOT fabricate zeros or a placeholder for an unavailable pair, as the return-shape note for this function already requires.
open_points.question: Must the note name the enum members exactly as AVAILABLE, NOT_CONFIGURED and TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE, or are the lowercase strings intended to be additional member names?
